Set the reference level to the control condition explicitly rather than relying on alphabetical ordering

steps.description: Run DESeq2 differential expression on the raw gene-level counts (12,000 genes x 10 samples) with design ~condition, contrasting the treated level against the control level as named in metadata.csv, so that a positive log2 fold change means higher in treated. steps.name: DE diagnostics and visualisation
caveats: A p-value histogram with a peak away from zero, or a U shape, indicates model misspecification or unmodelled structure and must be reported rather than smoothed over

steps.question: Do the treated-vs-control DESeq2 results behave statistically, and what do the top differential genes look like across the 10 samples?
constraints: Plot the heatmap on VST (or rlog) values, never on raw counts

Do not relabel or re-threshold the DE results; consume the tables from T1S2 as written

steps.description: Generate diagnostic and communication figures for both DE fits from T1S2. Produce: raw p-value histograms for the full and sample_03-excluded designs (the check that the null is uniform and the FDR is interpretable); MA plots on shrunk log2 fold changes with padj<0.05 genes highlighted; volcano plots (shrunk log2FC vs -log10 padj) labelling the top 20 genes by adjusted p-value; a scatter of Wald statistics from the full design against the sample_03-excluded design with the diagonal drawn; and a VST-scale heatmap (row-centred) of the top 30 genes of the primary design across all 10 samples, with sample_03 marked in the column annotation alongside condition. acceptance_criteria: P-value histograms produced for both designs, with an explicit verdict on their shape (uniform / anti-conservative / anomalous)
MA and volcano plots produced for both designs using apeglm-shrunk log2 fold changes, with significance threshold stated on the figure
Statistic-vs-statistic scatter between the two designs saved, with its Spearman rho annotated
Heatmap of the top 30 genes of the primary design over all 10 samples, row-centred, with both condition and an 'is sample_03' annotation track
Numeric summary of up/down counts at padj<0.05 in the treated direction, using the condition level names from metadata.csv

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of the treated-vs-control signature
caveats: If the required human gene set collections are not present in the environment at run time, report the absence explicitly and deliver the DE results without pathway annotation — the research question is answered by T1S2 and survives the loss of this step

GO BP parent/child overlap means a raw count of significant sets overstates the number of independent findings — collapse redundant sets before reporting a headline number
steps.context: Interpretation layer for the primary question. GSEA is used rather than over-representation because with n=5 per group the FDR-significant gene list may be small or empty, and a rank-based test still uses the whole ranking. steps.question: Which biological processes and hallmark programmes are coordinately shifted between the treated and control muscle samples?
constraints: Rank on the full tested gene list; do not run enrichment on a thresholded significant-gene list only
Use human (Homo sapiens, HGNC symbol) gene set collections only — never the mouse or rat GMTs staged alongside them
Report BH-adjusted p-values computed within each collection separately, and state that GO BP sets are a nested hierarchy so significant hits will be heavily correlated
Do not run enrichment on the ranking if fewer than ~2,000 genes remain after universe intersection and identifier mapping; report the shortfall instead
steps.description: Run rank-based gene set enrichment (GSEA, e.g. fgsea) on the primary-design results from T1S2, ranking all tested genes by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (or by -log10(pvalue) signed by log2 fold change if the statistic is unavailable) — not by a truncated significant-gene list. Identifier space of counts.csv row names is reported (symbols vs Ensembl vs other) along with the mapping rate to HGNC symbols if mapping was needed
Hallmark GSEA repeated on the non-primary design's ranking, with a statement of which hallmark sets are significant in both, in only one, or in neither
If no gene set reaches adjusted p < 0.05, this is reported plainly with the top sets by nominal p clearly labelled as not passing FDR

plan.title: Treated vs control muscle DE with sample_03 outlier sensitivity
plan.analytical_narrative:
The dataset is a small, clean two-group bulk RNA-seq experiment: gene-level Salmon counts for 12,000 genes x 10 samples (counts.csv), with a 10-row metadata table carrying a single `condition` column (5 treated vs 5 control), unpaired, single batch, human skeletal muscle. The research question is simply which genes differ between the two conditions — but the profile already flags that sample_03 separates from every other sample on PCA and on the sample-distance heatmap, and with n=5 per group a single aberrant library can both create and destroy DE calls. The plan is therefore built around making the outlier decision explicitly and auditably rather than silently.

T1S1 characterises sample_03 quantitatively — library size, detected genes, per-sample count distributions, Cook's-distance-based outlier flags from the DESeq2 fit, robust sample correlations, and PCA on VST data with and without it — so that the separation is attributed to a concrete cause (depth, complexity, contamination-like expression shift) instead of being called an outlier because it is far away on a plot. The step deliberately does not remove anything; it produces the evidence and a recommendation.

T1S2 is the primary contrast, DESeq2 negative-binomial Wald on raw counts with `~condition`, treated vs control, run TWICE on the same filtered matrix: the full n=5/5 design and the sensitivity design with sample_03 dropped (n=4 or 5 depending on its group). Both result tables are reported side by side with a concordance analysis, and one is nominated as primary with the reason stated. This is the honest way to answer the question given a flagged sample: the reader sees how much of the answer depends on that one library. Because counts are Salmon-derived gene-level counts and the profile explicitly says it is not recorded whether length correction was applied, the step must not re-apply any length correction and must state this assumption.

T1S3 produces the diagnostic and communication plots — MA, volcano, p-value histograms for both designs, and a heatmap of top genes — which are also the check on whether the FDR machinery behaved (a non-uniform null p-value histogram would invalidate the gene list).

T2S1 takes the ranked gene list from the primary design into pathway-level interpretation with GSEA against the human hallmark and GO-BP collections staged in the environment (HGNC symbols). This is a supporting layer, not the answer: if the DE list is small or the sensitivity analysis shows it is outlier-driven, the enrichment step must say so rather than narrate a story. If the gene identifiers in counts.csv turn out to be Ensembl rather than symbols, the step maps via the staged human UniProt ID mapping or an installed annotation package, reporting the mapping rate.

No translational, biomarker, deconvolution, or drug steps are planned: the question asks only which genes differ, there are no outcome, exposure, or compound data, and n=5/5 cannot support predictive modelling.

Enrichment on an outlier-driven ranking will produce confident-looking pathways; if T1S2's concordance analysis showed the two designs disagree substantially, state that the pathway calls inherit that instability
GO BP parent/child overlap means a raw count of significant sets overstates the number of independent findings — collapse redundant sets before reporting a headline number
